## 🤖 Overview

The AI RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) API service provides intelligent search capabilities for Enterprise Architecture documentation. It combines semantic search with large language models to deliver contextual, conversational answers to questions about EA practices, patterns, and guidelines.

This service follows the **[Enterprise Architecture Standards](../../../../standards/application/)** including:

- **[Python Coding Standards](../../../../standards/technology/python/STD-TEC-PY-001-coding.md)** - Code quality, formatting, and best practices
- **[Python Microservice Implementation Standards](../../../../standards/technology/python/STD-TEC-PY-004-microservice-implementation.md)** - FastAPI patterns and architecture
- **[API Design Standards](../../../../standards/application/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md)** - RESTful design and consistency

The core component handles document ingestion, vector embeddings, semantic search, and AI-powered response generation. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Content Sources" GIT["📚 Git Repositories"] WIKI["📖 Wiki Systems"] DOCS["📄 Document Stores"] APIs["🔌 Content APIs"] end subgraph "RAG Service Container" API["🚀 FastAPI Service

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#eap-implementation-architecture] ### EAP Implementation Architecture **EAP-Specific Implementation**: Our Enterprise Architecture Practice uses MkDocs documentation as the primary content source, with this RAG Service API as an additional component that indexes the content into a vector database and enables natural language search with AI-generated responses. The service is deployed on EKS using AWS Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Sonnet for responses, Titan for embeddings) and OpenSearch, integrating with the existing MkDocs frontend via shared ALB routing. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend Layer" EA["🏛️ EA Reference (MkDocs)"] HEADER["📍 Header Quick Search"] ARIA_PAGE["🔍 ARIA Search Page"] end subgraph "EKS Cluster - Internal Services" ALB[🌐 AWS Load Balancer] subgraph "Shared Namespace (eap-reference-architecture-docs)" MKDOCS["📚 MkDocs Pods
(Frontend Only)"] RAG["📡 RAG API Pods
(2 replicas)"] QUICK_EP["/api/rag/v1/quick-search"] ARIA_EP["/api/rag/v1/search"] end end subgraph "AWS External Services" subgraph "AWS Bedrock Service" BEDROCK_API["🤖 AWS Bedrock API"] CLAUDE["🧠 Claude 3.5 Sonnet"] TITAN["📝 Amazon Titan"] LLAMA["🦙 Meta Llama"] COHERE["💫 Cohere Command"] end subgraph "OpenSearch Service" OPENSEARCH_API["🔍 OpenSearch API"] OS1["🔍 OpenSearch Node 1"] OS2["🔍 OpenSearch Node 2"] end end subgraph "External Services" subgraph "GitHub" GIT["📚 gainwell/eap-ref-architecture"] end end subgraph "Manual Workflow" DEPLOY[🚀 Website Deployment] --> REFRESH[📞 POST /api/v1/refresh] REFRESH --> INDEX[🔄 POST /api/rag/v1/index] end %% Frontend to API EA --> HEADER EA --> ARIA_PAGE HEADER -.->|"GET /api/rag/v1/quick-search
(keyword only)"| ALB ARIA_PAGE -.->|"POST /api/rag/v1/search
(AI-powered)"| ALB ALB --> MKDOCS ALB --> RAG RAG --> QUICK_EP RAG --> ARIA_EP %% Internal EKS Communication to External Services QUICK_EP -.->|"Keyword Search
(no embeddings)"| OPENSEARCH_API ARIA_EP -.->|"Vector Search
(with embeddings)"| OPENSEARCH_API %% Manual refresh workflow (RAG service pulls content) REFRESH -.->|"fetches content"| GIT INDEX -.->|"processes & embeds"| RAG RAG -.->|"Vector Embeddings
(IRSA/IAM)"| OPENSEARCH_API %% External AI Services (via Bedrock API) - only for ARIA search ARIA_EP -.->|"Embedding & Response Generation
(IRSA/IAM)"| BEDROCK_API RAG -.->|"Embedding & Response Generation
(IRSA/IAM)"| BEDROCK_API %% Bedrock model routing (specific use cases) BEDROCK_API -->|"Response Generation"| CLAUDE BEDROCK_API -->|"Text Embeddings"| TITAN BEDROCK_API -.->|available| LLAMA BEDROCK_API -.->|available| COHERE %% OpenSearch internal routing OPENSEARCH_API --> OS1 OPENSEARCH_API --> OS2 classDef frontend fill:#e1f5fe classDef api fill:#f3e5f5 classDef workflow fill:#fff3e0 classDef storage fill:#ffebee classDef external fill:#e8f5e8 classDef selected fill:#c8e6c9 classDef embeddings fill:#e8f5e8 classDef github fill:#f0f0f0 classDef endpoint fill:#ffe0b2 class EA,HEADER,ARIA_PAGE frontend class RAG,ALB,MKDOCS api class QUICK_EP,ARIA_EP endpoint class DEPLOY,REFRESH,INDEX workflow class OPENSEARCH_API,OS1,OS2 storage class BEDROCK_API,LLAMA,COHERE external class GIT github class CLAUDE selected class TITAN embeddings ``` **EAP Technology Choices:** - **Content Source**: Enterprise Architecture documentation via GitHub repository (`gainwell/eap-ref-architecture`) - RAG service pulls directly from Git, not MkDocs container - **Vector Database**: OpenSearch for enterprise search capabilities with IRSA authentication - **LLM Providers**: AWS Bedrock with IRSA authentication and specific model usage: - **Claude 3.5 Sonnet**: Conversational response generation - **Amazon Titan**: Text embeddings for vector search - **Deployment**: EKS with shared ALB for integration with existing infrastructure - **Security**: IRSA for AWS service access, path-based routing for CORS simplification

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#user-search-flow] ### User Search Flow **User Query Sequence**: This diagram shows how an end user searches for information using the EA Reference site, demonstrating the real-time AI-powered search experience. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User as 🧑‍💻 End User participant Browser as 🌐 Browser participant ALB as ⚖️ AWS Load Balancer participant MkDocs as 📚 MkDocs Pods participant RAG as 📡 RAG API Pods participant OpenSearch as 🔍 OpenSearch API participant OS1 as 🔍 OS Node 1 participant OS2 as 🔍 OS Node 2 participant Bedrock as 🤖 AWS Bedrock API participant Titan as 📝 Titan Embedding v2 participant Claude as 🧠 Claude 3.5 Sonnet Note over User, Claude: Interactive Documentation Search Experience %% Initial page load User ->> Browser: Opens EA Reference documentation site Browser ->> ALB: HTTPS request to
ea-reference. ALB ->> MkDocs: Route to MkDocs frontend MkDocs -->> ALB: Return documentation page
with search interface ALB -->> Browser: Serve EA documentation page Note over User, Claude: User submits search query %% User search interaction User ->> Browser: Types: "What are enterprise
architecture principles?" Browser ->> ALB: POST /api/rag/v1/search (HTTPS/CORS) ALB ->> RAG: Route API request to RAG service Note over RAG, Claude: Query Embedding & Vector Search %% Query embedding generation first RAG ->> Bedrock: Convert query to vector embedding (IRSA/IAM) Bedrock ->> Titan: Generate embedding for user query Titan -->> Bedrock: Return query vector embedding Bedrock -->> RAG: Query embedding ready for search %% Vector similarity search using query embedding RAG ->> OpenSearch: Vector similarity search
with query embedding (IRSA/IAM) par Parallel OpenSearch Query OpenSearch ->> OS1: Query vector embeddings and OpenSearch ->> OS2: Query vector embeddings end par Parallel Response Collection OS1 -->> OpenSearch: Return relevant document chunks and OS2 -->> OpenSearch: Return relevant document chunks end OpenSearch -->> RAG: Aggregated results with relevance scores Note over RAG, Claude: AI Response Generation %% AI response generation with retrieved context RAG ->> Bedrock: Request contextual response with retrieved docs (IRSA/IAM) Bedrock ->> Claude: Generate answer with search context Claude -->> Bedrock: Return conversational response Bedrock -->> RAG: AI-generated answer with citations %% Response delivery RAG -->> ALB: JSON response (answer + sources + metadata) ALB -->> Browser: Return search results Note over User, Claude: Search completed with contextual answer and citations ```

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#content-management-flow]

### Content Management Flow

**Administrative Workflow**: This diagram shows the content refresh and indexing process that can be triggered by website deployments, RAG service deployments, or manual invocations, demonstrating how new documentation becomes searchable.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Admin as 👨‍💼 Administrator
    participant GitHub as � GitHub Repository
    participant Actions as ⚙️ GitHub Actions
    participant Runner as 🏃‍♂️ Actions Runner
    participant kubectl as ☸️ kubectl (port-forward)
    participant RAG as � RAG API Pods
    participant Bedrock as 🤖 AWS Bedrock API
    participant Titan as 📝 Titan Embedding v2
    participant OpenSearch as 🔍 OpenSearch API
    participant OS1 as 🔍 OS Node 1
    participant OS2 as 🔍 OS Node 2

    Note over Admin, OS2: Content Refresh & Indexing Workflow

    %% GitHub workflow trigger
    Admin ->> GitHub: Merge content changes to main branch
    GitHub ->> Actions: Trigger deploy workflow
    Actions ->> Runner: Start runner with EKS access

    Note over Runner, RAG: Step 1: Content Preparation

    %% Content preparation phase - runner does the work
    Runner->>GitHub: Clone repository locally
    Note over GitHub: gainwell/eap-ref-architecture
    GitHub-->>Runner: Repository cloned to runner
    Runner->>Runner: Filter and prepare published content
    Runner->>Runner: Create content manifest with file paths and metadata

    Note over Runner, RAG: Step 2: Content Indexing via kubectl

    %% Content indexing phase via kubectl port-forward with prepared content
    Runner->>kubectl: kubectl port-forward rag-service:8443
    kubectl->>RAG: Establish port-forward tunnel
    Runner->>kubectl: POST /api/rag/v1/index with content manifest (via port-forward)
    kubectl->>RAG: Route indexing request with prepared content to RAG service
    RAG-->>kubectl: Indexing started (async operation)
    kubectl-->>Runner: Return indexing request acknowledgment
    Runner-->>Actions: Deployment workflow completed

    Note over RAG: Asynchronous background processing
    RAG->>RAG: Process provided content and extract chunks

    %% Vector embedding generation (background)
    RAG ->> Bedrock: Generate embeddings for new content (IRSA/IAM)
    Bedrock ->> Titan: Create vector embeddings for text chunks
    Titan -->> Bedrock: Return vector embeddings
    Bedrock -->> RAG: Embedding vectors ready for storage

    %% Vector storage distribution (background)
    RAG ->> OpenSearch: Store vector embeddings (IRSA/IAM)
    par Parallel Vector Storage
        OpenSearch ->> OS1: Store embedding vectors
    and
        OpenSearch ->> OS2: Store embedding vectors
    end

    par Parallel Storage Confirmation
        OS1 -->> OpenSearch: Confirm storage completion
    and
        OS2 -->> OpenSearch: Confirm storage completion
    end

    OpenSearch -->> RAG: All embeddings successfully indexed
    Actions -->> GitHub: Content now searchable via RAG

    Note over Admin, OS2: New content is now available for AI-powered search
```

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#component-architecture]

### Component Architecture

```text
AI RAG API Service (Current Implementation)
├── FastAPI Backend           # REST API with async support
├── RAG Search Engine         # LangChain + OpenSearch integration
├── Document Processor        # Content indexing and metadata extraction
├── Git Content Manager       # Repository synchronization
├── Authentication Service    # 📋 Future feature (module exists, not integrated)
└── Rate Limiter             # 📋 Future feature (module exists, not integrated)
```

**Core API Endpoints:**

- `POST /api/rag/v1/search` - AI-powered conversational search with LLM-generated responses
- `GET /api/rag/v1/quick-search` - Fast keyword-only search for header "Quick Search" (<200ms)
- `POST /api/rag/v1/index` - Manual content indexing (administrative operation)
- `POST /api/v1/refresh` - Manual Git content refresh (administrative operation)

**Search Architecture**: The service provides two search modes:

- **Quick Search** (`/rag/quick-search`): Fast keyword matching without LLM processing, used by MkDocs header search
- **ARIA Search** (`/rag/search`): Full RAG with Claude 3.5 Sonnet for conversational responses

**Architecture Decision**: Single service with manual refresh workflow. Content is refreshed via API calls triggered by website deployments rather than background scheduled tasks. The RAG service handles all content management operations and securely connects to AWS services (OpenSearch and Bedrock) using IRSA authentication.

**For detailed architecture information**, see the [Architecture Guide](docs/architecture.md).

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#search-modes]

### Search Modes

The RAG service provides two complementary search modes, both powered by OpenSearch:
page_texts.13:
[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#1-quick-search-get-apiragv1quick-search]

#### 1. Quick Search (`GET /api/rag/v1/quick-search`)

**Purpose**: Fast document lookup for the MkDocs header search bar

**Characteristics**:

- **Speed**: <200ms response time target
- **Technology**: Keyword matching against OpenSearch index
- **No AI**: Direct keyword search without LLM processing
- **Use Case**: Quick reference lookup while browsing documentation
- **Client**: MkDocs platform header search (JavaScript integration)

**Example Response**:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Enterprise Architecture Principles",
      "url": "/guiding-principles/core/",
      "excerpt": "Core principles guide all EA decisions...",
      "score": 0.95
    }
  ],
  "total_results": 1,
  "response_time_ms": 120
}
```
page_texts.14:
[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#2-aria-search-post-apiragv1search]

#### 2. ARIA Search (`POST /api/rag/v1/search`)

**Purpose**: Conversational AI-powered search with contextual understanding

**Characteristics**:

- **Speed**: 5-15 second response time (includes LLM processing)
- **Technology**: OpenSearch retrieval + AWS Bedrock (Claude 3.5 Sonnet)
- **AI-Generated**: Contextual answers with source citations
- **Use Case**: Complex questions requiring explanation and context
- **Client**: Dedicated ARIA search page with full chat interface

**Example Response**:

```json
{
  "answer": "Enterprise Architecture principles at Gainwell...",
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "Core Principles",
      "url": "/guiding-principles/core/",
      "excerpt": "...",
      "relevance_score": 0.92
    }
  ],
  "conversation_id": "abc123",
  "response_time_ms": 8450,
  "confidence_score": 0.88
}
```
page_texts.15:
[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#architecture-benefits]

### Architecture Benefits

**Why Two Search Modes?**

- **Performance**: Quick search optimized for speed, ARIA for quality
- **User Experience**: Right tool for the right task (lookup vs. learning)
- **Resource Efficiency**: LLM calls only when needed
- **Single Source**: Both use the same OpenSearch index (consistency)
page_texts.16:
[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#currently-implemented]

### Currently Implemented

- **Conversational Search**: Natural language queries with contextual AI responses (Claude 3.5 Sonnet)
- **Quick Keyword Search**: Fast document lookup for header search (<200ms, no LLM)
- **Hybrid Search**: Combines semantic similarity with keyword matching
- **Source Attribution**: Every response includes citations and links
- **Multi-turn Dialogue**: Maintains conversation context
- **Domain Filtering**: Search within specific architecture domains
- **Health Monitoring**: Comprehensive health checks and statistics
- **Graceful Degradation**: Falls back to mock responses when AI services unavailable
- **Unified Architecture**: Single OpenSearch backend serves both search modes

## 🚀 Production Deployment

**This service is deployed via the dedicated RAG service workflow** which handles RAG service deployment and integration with the shared infrastructure.

**Deployment Process:**

1. **Dedicated Workflow**: RAG service uses `deploy-rag-service.yml` for deployment
2. **Shared Infrastructure**: Integrates with existing MKDocs ALB and EKS cluster
3. **GitHub Actions**: Automated deployment via dedicated RAG service workflow
4. **SSL Support**: End-to-end HTTPS with dual HTTP/HTTPS port configuration

**Manual Trigger (for development):**

- Navigate to GitHub Actions → "Deploy RAG Service" → "Run workflow"
- Select deployment target (dev/prod) and trigger manually

**For complete deployment details**, see the [Deployment Guide](docs/deployment.md).

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#common-issues]

#### **Common Issues**

| Issue                     | Symptoms                  | Solution                             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **OpenSearch Connection** | `ConnectionError` in logs | Check `ea-opensearch` service status |
| **AWS Bedrock Access**    | `AccessDeniedException`   | Verify IRSA role permissions         |
| **CORS Errors**           | Frontend can't access API | Check `CORS_ORIGINS` configuration   |
| **Pod Startup Issues**    | `CrashLoopBackOff`        | Check resource limits and secrets    |

**Deployment Note**:

- Administrative endpoints (`/api/rag/v1/index`, `/api/v1/refresh`) should typically be configured with restricted network access for security.
- CORS issues can be avoided by using shared ALB path-based routing (`/api/rag/v1/*`) where the API appears to be from the same domain as the frontend.

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#irsa-troubleshooting-for-search-failures]

#### **IRSA Troubleshooting for Search Failures**

If `/api/rag/v1/search` calls fail after initially working, check these common IRSA issues:

1. **Token Expiration**: IRSA tokens expire after ~1 hour

   ```bash
   # Check token status
   kubectl exec -n eap-reference-architecture-docs deployment/ea-rag-service -- \
     aws sts get-caller-identity
   ```

2. **Role ARN Mismatch**: Verify service account annotation

   ```bash
   kubectl get serviceaccount -n eap-reference-architecture-docs rag-service-account -o yaml
   ```

3. **IAM Trust Policy**: Check OIDC provider configuration

   ```bash
   aws iam get-role --role-name ${RESOURCE_PREFIX}-eap-rag-service --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument'
   ```

4. **Permission Issues**: Verify Bedrock and OpenSearch policies

   ```bash
   aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name ${RESOURCE_PREFIX}-eap-rag-service
   ```

5. **Health Endpoint Check**: Monitor AWS credential status via HTTPS

   ```bash
   # External health check via ingress (HTTPS with SSL termination)
   curl -s https://ea-reference.shared.dev.pgwcloud.net/api/v1/health | jq '.components.aws_credentials'

   # Internal health check via pod HTTPS (self-signed certificate)
   kubectl exec -n eap-reference-architecture-docs deployment/ea-rag-service -- \
     curl -k -s https://localhost:8443/health | jq '.components.aws_credentials'
   ```

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#architecture-note-https-first-design]

#### **Architecture Note: HTTPS-First Design**

The RAG service uses **HTTPS (port 8443)** as the primary protocol:

- **Ingress**: ALB terminates SSL and forwards HTTPS traffic to pod port 8443
- **Health Probes**: Kubernetes uses HTTPS on port 8443 (with self-signed certificates)
- **HTTP Port 8080**: Available for internal debugging but not exposed via ingress

[.tooling/components/apis/rag-service/README.md#security-considerations]

### **Security Considerations**

- **Simplified Access Model**: No authentication required for search endpoints - designed for internal company use
- **IRSA Integration**: Secure AWS service access without hardcoded credentials:
    - **AWS Bedrock**: For embedding generation and response generation
    - **AWS OpenSearch**: For vector storage and retrieval operations
- **CORS Configuration**: Configurable CORS middleware for cross-origin access control
- **GitHub Access**: Public repository access, no authentication required for content fetching

**Recommended Deployment**: Administrative endpoints (`/api/rag/v1/index`, `/api/v1/refresh`) should be deployed with restricted access (e.g., internal-only network access) as they perform content management operations.
